findings.quote: It was Marcos admitting, in that single sentence, that sometimes a ten-year-old needs a direct answer, that circling isn t always enough
findings.claim: The narrator explains in adult abstractions what the scene has just delivered, handing the child a conclusion instead of a discovery.
findings.fix: Keep the plainness that angered him; cut the maxim.

findings.quote: and found in them what had always been there: a man who believed in him so completely that he would let him be frightened to prove it.
findings.claim: The last line tells the child what to feel at the exact moment it should be showing him.

findings.quote: That was Bruno s way of saying that things were confusing and frightening, but that he was staying right there anyway
findings.claim: Three translations of Bruno s behaviour in three paragraphs turn the dog into a device the narrator speaks through.
findings.fix: Keep the actions, cut two of the three translations.

iterations.notes: both majors and the minor resolved; no new defect. The critic checked the two seams the cuts risked - whether the anger paragraph is now too bare and whether Neither of them looked away is too flat a last line - and cleared both, calling the new ending the right note to land on.
